claim: REVIEW-r4a finding #3 re-flags decision 4 ('identity never from the connection') only against the 2025-xx #542/#539 case, but r2 and r3 already found and the current ADR-0007 text still carries a deeper, unfixed problem: in the 2026-07-28 spec itself, the request-side clientInfo _meta key is OPTIONAL and the spec tells servers not to use it to change behaviour, so a 2026-07-28 client can send no client identity at all. Decision 4 as written ('from request _meta ... never from the connection') has no fallback for that case, meaning ctx_doctor's 'clientInfo = agent' check and ctx_upgrade's #542 platform-threading fix have NO working mechanism for any 2026-07-28 client, not just a narrower 2025-xx regression. This was already found at major/blocker severity in round 3 (out/r3/A/round1/review/mcp.json) with a stated fix (a server-assigned --agent flag from adapters/table.ts instead of relying on clientInfo at all) and was never carried into DECISIONS-r3.md's accepted Q1-Q19 list, and the ADR-0007 file on disk is byte-identical to the version r3 flagged. Pass A's r4a #3 is therefore an under-scoped restatement of an already-deeper, still-open finding, not a new one.
evidence: docs/v2/adr/0007-mcp-2026-07-28.md:47 (current text, unchanged); docs/v2/review/out/r3/A/round1/review/mcp.json line 2: "the _meta clientInfo key is optional, and the spec says servers SHOULD NOT use it to change behaviour... v2 has no agent identity for platform-aware paths, ctx_doctor and ctx_upgrade", citing python-sdk/src/mcp-types/mcp_types/_v2026_07_28/__init__.py:2822-2836 ('io.modelcontextprotocol/clientInfo ... = None; Servers SHOULD NOT use it to change their behavior') and python-sdk/docs/whats-new.md:201; grep of docs/v2/review/DECISIONS-r3.md for 'clientInfo|identity|--agent' returns zero matches, confirming the r3 fix was never adopted as an owner decision; REVIEW-r4a.md line 11 (pass A finding #3) only cites cm-main 7e67952c/8b9d13a1 (#542/#539, both 2025-xx) and does not mention the 2026-07-28 optional-clientInfo gap at all.
archaeology: INTRODUCED_BY b40d6bdb 2026-03-16 'feat: add MCP clientInfo detection + Antigravity and Kiro adapters' (first use of clientInfo as the platform signal); 7e67952c 2026-05-12 'fix(detect): thread MCP clientInfo through ctx_upgrade to upgrade() (closes #542 partial — 3 of 6)' — commit message states 'clientInfo from the MCP handshake is the highest-confidence signal available' (src/server.ts ~4290-4293, read via server.server.getClientVersion()); 8b9d13a1 2026-05-12 'test(detect): pin MCP clientInfo priority over env-var detection (closes #539 partial)'. ORIGINAL_INTENT (7e67952c, quoted): 'detectPlatform() runs IN-PROCESS here (no spawn boundary) so clientInfo from the MCP handshake is the highest-confidence signal available.' REGRESSION_RISK: v1's whole #542/#539 fix series is built on clientInfo being reliably present; the 2026-07-28 spec makes that same field optional and tells servers to ignore it for behaviour changes, so a bare port of v1's detection logic to a 2026-07-28 session silently falls through to the lower-confidence config-dir heuristic tier that #542 was filed against in the first place — reopening #542 for every 2026-07-28 client, not just 2025-xx ones as r4a's narrower finding implies. SAFE_FIX_CONSTRAINTS: per r3's already-accepted-but-undocumented fix, identity for ctx_doctor/ctx_upgrade must come from a source adapters/table.ts assigns per agent (e.g. an --agent <id> argv flag baked into the generated MCP server entry at install time), with clientInfo used only for display/debug-report purposes, never as the sole detection path; this must be written into ADR-0007 decision 4 and into a DECISIONS-r3-style accepted row before implementation, and a GP1 case must cover a 2026-07-28 client that sends no clientInfo at all.
fix: Rewrite ADR-0007 decision 4 to: identity for platform-aware paths (ctx_doctor, ctx_upgrade) comes from an --agent <id> flag baked into the per-adapter MCP entry by adapters/table.ts at install time, not from clientInfo/_meta, because the 2026-07-28 spec makes clientInfo optional and non-behavioural; clientInfo (via initialize for 2025-xx, via _meta for 2026-07-28 when present) is used only for the debug report and ctx_stats display. Add this as an explicit accepted decision (not just a review finding) and add it to DECISIONS-r3.md's Q-list so it does not keep reappearing unresolved across rounds. Add a GP1 case: a 2026-07-28 client with no clientInfo at all still resolves the correct agent id for ctx_doctor/ctx_upgrade.

claim: ADR-0007's context table still says 'DiscoverResult carries supportedVersions, capabilities, serverInfo and instructions (schema.ts:678-696)'. Round 3 already found this placement wrong — in the 2026-07-28 schema, serverInfo was moved out of the DiscoverResult body and is instead stamped into every 2026-era result's _meta key (spec change #3002) — and that finding was never corrected in the ADR text on disk.
evidence: docs/v2/adr/0007-mcp-2026-07-28.md:13 (current text, unchanged, still lists serverInfo inside DiscoverResult); docs/v2/review/out/r3/A/round1/review/mcp.json line 4: "In the 2026-07-28 schema serverInfo moved out of the discover body into each result's _meta... DiscoverResult in python-sdk _v2026_07_28/__init__.py:2347-2400 has instructions, supportedVersions, ttlMs, cacheScope and no server_info field; serverInfo is a _meta key at lines 736 and 890"; GS9/TECH-SPEC.md:40 and ADR-0007's own Tests section ('Both runs must produce byte-identical instructions and tool lists') say nothing about serverInfo's location, so a GP1/GP2 test built against the ADR's current (wrong) schema description would assert on the wrong field.
archaeology: No v1 analog — serverInfo-in-_meta is new to the 2026-07-28 spec, so this is a doc-accuracy gap rather than a v1 regression. Not a case for the git-archaeology MUST-5 method (no v1 file/behaviour is implicated); flagging as a straight documentation correction carried forward unresolved from round 3.
fix: Correct the context table row: DiscoverResult carries supportedVersions, capabilities, instructions, ttlMs, cacheScope; serverInfo is read from the result's _meta key (io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo), not from the DiscoverResult body. Re-verify against schema.ts:678-696 directly and quote the exact field list in the ADR so GP1/GP2's byte-identical-result test checks the right location.
